messages:
dalia: Proposal: extract tenant admission & quota logic out of runtime into a tiny "coordinator" service. Goal is to centralize hierarchical quotas, admission policies, and per-tenant fairshare while keeping runtime focused on token generation.

mike: Curious — why not keep quotas as a runtime sidecar? We already have local token buckets per-node that are cheap.

dalia: Two reasons: 1) cross-tenant fairness and burst coordination are messy if every node decides locally (we get head-of-line unfairness), 2) feature velocity: product wants weighted preemption, burst credits, and time-windowed promos — easier to implement once in a single place.

anya: Risk: adding a coordinator in the critical path could increase tail latency. How do you avoid becoming the latency bottleneck?

dalia: Plan: keep coordinator out of the hot path for happy-path requests via two modes: async-allowed and strict-admit. Default is async-allowed where runtime consults a cached decision and proceeds; coordinator receives events and updates caches. Strict-admit mode (opt-in tenants / surcharge calls) requires a fast sync check. Both use signed admission-tokens to avoid replay.

sasha: Cache invalidation complexity. If coordinator updates a tenant's quota (promo), we need near-instant invalidation so runtimes don't continue allowing bursts. How are you handling TTLs and push invalidation?

dalia: Hybrid: caches with short TTLs (250ms) plus a push invalidation channel over the internal pubsub for immediate revokes. For private/on-prem, pubsub falls back to a small agent that exposes an HTTP callback. We'll measure invalidation lag and provide metrics.

elaine: What about durability of tenancy state? We need audit trails and owner history for enterprise customers. Coordinator must persist change logs and support replay.

dalia: Coordinator will write policy changes to our control-plane DB (append-only events). For local runtime caches we keep small pointers (policy_version). Replays are used for incident recovery.

quota-bot: quota-bot: current cluster quota window consumption: 72% of steady-state; per-tenant top-3: acme(24%), beta-inc(18%), redwood-qa(12%).

mike: How to migrate? If we flip coordinator on for a tenant and something goes wrong we need safe rollback. Also how to handle region affinity — customers in EU shouldn't be funneled through NA control plane.

dalia: Migration plan: 1) Read-only deploy: coordinator observes and publishes decisions but runtimes ignore (1 sprint). 2) Cache-assisted mode: runtimes use cached decisions and emit telemetry (2 sprints). 3) Opt-in tenants with strict-admit for sensitive customers (4 weeks). 4) Global roll with region-local coordinator instances and geo-aware routing (2 sprints). Rollback is a single toggle per-region that tells runtimes to ignore coordinator decisions and use local heuristics.

sasha: Geo-local coordinators means state sync. Do we plan eventual consistency or strongly consistent policy updates?

dalia: Policies are mostly eventual-consistent (promos and weights can take small time to converge). For billing-critical limits (hard caps) we do strongly-consistent checks via a fast-path RAFT group limited to the tenant's shards. We'll avoid global RAFT for scale reasons.

anya: From an implementation POV: what API surface does runtime need? I assume: checkAdmission(tenant, tokensNeeded, mode) -> {decision, token?} and a streaming invalidation channel.

dalia: Exactly. Example:

POST /v1/admit { tenant_id: "acme", tokens: 32, mode: "async" } -> 200 { decision: "allow", token: "ad-xx", policy_version: "v12" }

Runtime uses token with request metadata so later audits can link usage to admission decisions. If decision == "defer", runtime can queue locally or fall back to best-effort pool.

mike: Auditing & compliance notes: store token signatures and policy_version in traces. Also provide an API to export per-tenant admission logs for X days (configurable).

dalia: Will add retention settings and HSM-signed tokens for private deployments.

elaine: Alerting/SLAs for coordinator? If coordinator degrades, we must not take down customers. What's the safe default?

dalia: Safe defaults: 1) If coordinator unreachable, runtimes switch to local heuristics and enter degraded mode with conservative limits. 2) Expose a degraded boolean in /health endpoints. 3) Pager only if degraded plus admission_fail_rate > threshold.

sasha: Perf targets? We should aim for coordinator RT < 2ms for sync checks (in-region) and invalidation latency < 50ms for push channel. If we can't hit these, keep coordinator out of hot path.

mike: Test plan: synthetic traffic that mirrors real tenant mixes + heavy burst scenarios (+ tool-calling flows). Run chaos tests where pubsub messages drop and coordinator restarts. Verify no tenant starvation.

dalia: Ownership: I'll author RFC and coord prototype. Mike -> telemetry & tracing, Sasha -> invalidation & geo-agent, Elaine -> rollout/runbook and compliance hooks.

quota-bot: quota-bot: noted owners: dalia,mike,sasha,elaine. CI: coord-proto branch pushed.

anya: One more ask: include a small SDK shim for runtime teams so adoption is frictionless. Keep runtime dependency minimal (HTTP + tiny cache lib).

dalia: Yep, lightweight shim + example integration for python/go/node. I'll include that in the RFC. Planning to open RFC tomorrow.

mike: +1. Also add a dashboard: "admission_token_miss_rate" and "coordinator_degraded_mode" per-region, per-tenant.

dalia: Will add. Thanks everyone — I'll draft the RFC and share the diagram and API examples.
